pharm: Oral inhibitor of HIF-2α that blocks the HIF-2α-HIF-1β interaction, reducing transcription of genes for proliferation, angiogenesis and tumor growth that are driven by loss of VHL protein function. Used for VHL disease-associated tumors and for advanced renal cell carcinoma after a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and a VEGF-TKI.

summary: Belzutifan (WELIREG) is an oral HIF-2α inhibitor given at 120 mg once daily. It is indicated for adults with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease who need treatment for associated renal cell carcinoma, CNS hemangioblastomas or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors that do not need immediate surgery, and for adults with advanced renal cell carcinoma after a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and a VEGF tyrosine kinase inhibitor. It carries a boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity. Anemia and hypoxia are the main toxicities and set the dose modifications; it can also make hormonal contraceptives ineffective.
indications: Adults with von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease who require therapy for associated renal cell carcinoma (RCC), central nervous system (CNS) hemangioblastomas, or pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (pNET), not requiring immediate surgery
Adults with advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) following a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor and a vascular endothelial growth factor tyrosine kinase inhibitor (VEGF-TKI)

Swallow tablets whole; do not chew, crush or split them

moa: Belzutifan is an inhibitor of hypoxia-inducible factor 2 alpha (HIF-2α), a transcription factor that regulates oxygen-sensing genes. With normal oxygen, VHL protein targets HIF-2α for ubiquitin-proteasomal degradation; without functional VHL protein, HIF-2α accumulates, enters the nucleus, pairs with HIF-1β and switches on genes for proliferation, angiogenesis and tumor growth. Belzutifan binds HIF-2α and blocks the HIF-2α-HIF-1β interaction, reducing transcription of those genes. It also suppresses erythropoietin production, which explains the anemia (plasma erythropoietin fell about 60% from baseline after 2 weeks).

relative: Pregnancy: boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity; verify pregnancy status and use effective non-hormonal contraception
Breastfeeding: do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose
Concomitant UGT2B17 or CYP2C19 inhibitors, or dual UGT2B17 and CYP2C19 poor metabolizers (higher belzutifan exposure)
Concomitant sensitive CYP3A4 substrates (their exposure falls; avoid if a small decrease could cause treatment failure)
Pre-existing anemia or low oxygen saturation (both are common on treatment; monitor closely)
monitor: Oxygen saturation before starting and periodically (rest and exercise)
Signs of hemorrhage and visual changes

preg: Boxed warning: exposure during pregnancy can cause embryo-fetal harm. In rats, belzutifan caused embryo-fetal lethality, reduced fetal body weight and fetal skeletal malformations at exposures of about 0.2 times the human exposure or more. There are no data in pregnant women. Verify pregnancy status before starting. Females of reproductive potential should use effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose, because belzutifan can render some hormonal contraceptives ineffective. Males with female partners of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. It may impair fertility in males and females; reversibility is unknown.
lact: There are no data on belzutifan or its metabolites in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed child, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
renal: No dosage modification is recommended in mild (eGFR 60-89) or moderate (eGFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m2) renal impairment. It has not been studied in severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29). Note that creatinine commonly rises on treatment (64% in VHL disease, 34% in advanced RCC).
hepatic: No dosage modification is recommended in mild hepatic impairment (total bilirubin at or below the upper limit of normal with AST above normal, or bilirubin up to 1.5 times normal with any AST). It has not been studied in moderate or severe hepatic impairment (total bilirubin above 1.5 times normal with any AST).

major: Hormonal contraceptives - belzutifan can cause contraceptive failure or more breakthrough bleeding; use effective non-hormonal contraception

Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates (for example midazolam) - belzutifan lowers their concentrations (midazolam AUC fell 40%, and is predicted to fall up to 70% in dual poor metabolizers); avoid, or increase the substrate dose per its own label if it cannot be avoided
moderate: UGT2B17 or CYP2C19 inhibitors - raise belzutifan exposure and may increase anemia and hypoxia; monitor for both and reduce the belzutifan dose as recommended

Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents - safety in VHL disease treated with belzutifan is not established; in cancer patients on myelosuppressive chemotherapy, ESAs increased the risk of death and serious cardiovascular reactions (see the ESA label)
minor: In vitro, belzutifan is a substrate of P-gp, OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 and inhibits MATE2K; clinical relevance is not stated in the label
interactions.food: A high-fat, high-calorie meal delayed Tmax by about 2 hours with no clinically meaningful effect on Cmax or AUC; it may be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction stated in the label.
interactions.diagnostics: Lowers hemoglobin and suppresses erythropoietin; commonly raises creatinine and glucose and can change lymphocyte, sodium, potassium, ALT and AST values (see monitoring).

common: Decreased hemoglobin / anemia (93% VHL disease, 88% advanced RCC)
serious: Severe anemia requiring transfusion (Grade 3 in 7% VHL, 29% RCC)
Severe hypoxia (serious in 7% in advanced RCC); may need oxygen or hospitalization
Hemorrhage (3% serious in RCC), including intracranial hemorrhage (0.8%)
Pneumonia and pleural effusion (serious in 3.5% and 2.2% in RCC)
rare: Retinal detachment and central retinal vein occlusion (1 patient each in VHL disease; retinal detachment 0.3% in RCC)
Anaphylaxis reaction (1 patient in VHL disease)
emergency: Life-threatening anemia (hemoglobin below 8 g/dL or urgent intervention indicated)
Hypoxia at rest (pulse oximeter below 88% or PaO2 55 mm Hg or less) or life-threatening hypoxia

monitoring: Hemoglobin before starting and periodically throughout treatment
Oxygen saturation (pulse oximetry) before starting and periodically, including with exercise
Pregnancy status before starting in females of reproductive potential, and contraception counselling
Creatinine, glucose, liver enzymes, sodium and potassium as clinically indicated (common laboratory changes)
Visual symptoms and signs of bleeding
counsel: Take one tablet by mouth once a day at the same time each day, with or without food, and swallow it whole

Your blood count will be checked often because severe anemia is common and may need a transfusion; tell your care team about tiredness, feeling cold, shortness of breath, chest pain or a fast heartbeat
Low oxygen levels can be serious; get help right away for shortness of breath or a fast heart rate
You must not become pregnant: use effective non-hormonal birth control during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose; birth control pills, injections and patches may not work
Men with female partners who could become pregnant should use effective contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose
Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose
This medicine may affect fertility in men and women
If you miss a dose, take it the same day if you can; do not take extra tablets. If you vomit after a dose, do not take it again
pk: Steady state is reached after about 3 days; erythropoietin suppression peaks after about 2 weeks of dosing
Median Tmax 1 to 2 hours (about 2 hours later after a high-fat meal)
Mean elimination half-life about 14 hours; clearance about 6.0 L/hr
Volume of distribution about 119 L; plasma protein binding 45%
Mainly UGT2B17 and CYP2C19, to a lesser extent CYP3A4
About 49.6% in urine and 51.7% in feces, mostly as inactive metabolites
Store at 20-25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); keep in the original bottle with the desiccant canisters
pearls: Anemia is almost universal (93% in VHL disease, 88% in advanced RCC; Grade 3 in 7% and 29%) because belzutifan suppresses erythropoietin; check hemoglobin before starting and periodically. The safety of ESAs with belzutifan in VHL disease is not established
Hypoxia can be severe (15% in advanced RCC, 10% Grade 3): check oxygen saturation at rest and with exercise before and during treatment, and withhold for saturation below 88%
It can make hormonal contraceptives fail: use non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose

Pharmacogenomics matter: UGT2B17 poor metabolizers have 2.5-fold, CYP2C19 poor metabolizers 1.3-fold and dual poor metabolizers 3.2-fold higher exposure. The label notes up to 77% of certain Asian populations are UGT2B17 poor metabolizers, up to 19% CYP2C19 poor metabolizers and up to 15% dual poor metabolizers, so watch closely for anemia and hypoxia

Evidence: VHL-associated RCC ORR 49% (all partial responses), CNS hemangioblastomas 63%, pNET 83%. In advanced RCC (LITESPARK-005) versus everolimus: median PFS 5.6 vs 5.6 months (HR 0.75, p=0.0008), ORR 22% vs 4%; overall survival was immature
No clinically significant pharmacokinetic differences by age (19-90 years), sex, race, body weight (42-166 kg), or mild to moderate renal impairment
This record follows the 02/2024 US label; check the current label for any later indications or changes
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as possible on the same day, then resume the regular daily schedule the next day. Do not take extra tablets to make up for the missed dose. If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not retake it; take the next dose the next day.
overdose: There is no specific treatment for overdose. If overdose is suspected, withhold belzutifan and give supportive care. Grade 3 hypoxia occurred at 120 mg twice a day and Grade 4 thrombocytopenia at 240 mg once daily (about 2 times the recommended dosage).
